# toml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/toml/^0.9/

## Expand description

A [serde](https://serde.rs/)-compatible [TOML](https://github.com/toml-lang/toml)-parsing library

TOML itself is a simple, ergonomic, and readable configuration format:

```
[package]
name = "toml"
[dependencies]
serde = "1.0"
```
The TOML format tends to be relatively common throughout the Rust community
for configuration, notably being used by [Cargo](https://crates.io/), Rust’s package manager.

[§](https://docs.rs#toml-values)TOML values

A TOML document is represented with the [ Table](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html) type which maps

`String` to the [enum:](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html)

`Value````
pub enum Value {
   String(String),
   Integer(i64),
   Float(f64),
   Boolean(bool),
   Datetime(Datetime),
   Array(Array),
   Table(Table),
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-toml)Parsing TOML

The easiest way to parse a TOML document is via the [ Table](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html) type:

```
use toml::Table;
let value = "foo = 'bar'".parse::<Table>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(value["foo"].as_str(), Some("bar"));
```
The [ Table](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html) type implements a number of convenience methods and
traits; the example above uses

[to parse a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/traits/trait.FromStr.html)

`FromStr`[into a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`str`[.](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html)

`Table`[§](https://docs.rs#deserialization-and-serialization)Deserialization and Serialization

This crate supports [ serde](https://serde.rs/) 1.0 with a number of
implementations of the

`Deserialize`, `Serialize`, `Deserializer`, and
`Serializer` traits. Namely, you’ll find:- `Deserialize for Table`
- `Serialize for Table`
- `Deserialize for Value`
- `Serialize for Value`
- `Deserialize for Datetime`
- `Serialize for Datetime`
- `Deserializer for de::Deserializer`
- `Serializer for ser::Serializer`
- `Deserializer for Table`
- `Deserializer for Value`

This means that you can use Serde to deserialize/serialize the
[ Table](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html) type as well as

[and](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html)

`Value`[type in this crate. You can also use the](https://docs.rs/value/struct.Datetime.html)

`Datetime`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Deserializer.html)

`Deserializer`[, or](https://docs.rs/struct.Serializer.html)

`Serializer`[type itself to act as a deserializer/serializer for arbitrary types.](https://docs.rs/type.Table.html)

`Table`An example of deserializing with TOML is:

```
use serde::Deserialize;
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
   ip: String,
   port: Option<u16>,
   keys: Keys,
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Keys {
   github: String,
   travis: Option<String>,
}
let config: Config = toml::from_str(r#"
   ip = '127.0.0.1'
   [keys]
   github = 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx'
   travis = 'yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy'
"#).unwrap();
assert_eq!(config.ip, "127.0.0.1");
assert_eq!(config.port, None);
assert_eq!(config.keys.github, "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx");
assert_eq!(config.keys.travis.as_ref().unwrap(), "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy");
```
You can serialize types in a similar fashion:

```
use serde::Serialize;
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Config {
   ip: String,
   port: Option<u16>,
   keys: Keys,
}
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Keys {
   github: String,
   travis: Option<String>,
}
let config = Config {
   ip: "127.0.0.1".to_string(),
   port: None,
   keys: Keys {
       github: "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx".to_string(),
       travis: Some("yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy".to_string()),
   },
};
let toml = toml::to_string(&config).unwrap();
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Deserializing TOML into Rust structures.
- [map](https://docs.rs/map/index.html)
- A map of `String`to[Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html).
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)- `serde`
- Serializing Rust structures into TOML.

# tower_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tower-lsp/^0.20/

## Expand description

Language Server Protocol (LSP) server abstraction for [Tower](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use tower_lsp::jsonrpc::Result;
use tower_lsp::lsp_types::*;
use tower_lsp::{Client, LanguageServer, LspService, Server};
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Backend {
    client: Client,
}
#[tower_lsp::async_trait]
impl LanguageServer for Backend {
    async fn initialize(&self, _: InitializeParams) -> Result<InitializeResult> {
        Ok(InitializeResult {
            capabilities: ServerCapabilities {
                hover_provider: Some(HoverProviderCapability::Simple(true)),
                completion_provider: Some(CompletionOptions::default()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            ..Default::default()
        })
    }
    async fn initialized(&self, _: InitializedParams) {
        self.client
            .log_message(MessageType::INFO, "server initialized!")
            .await;
    }
    async fn shutdown(&self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
    async fn completion(&self, _: CompletionParams) -> Result<Option<CompletionResponse>> {
        Ok(Some(CompletionResponse::Array(vec![
            CompletionItem::new_simple("Hello".to_string(), "Some detail".to_string()),
            CompletionItem::new_simple("Bye".to_string(), "More detail".to_string())
        ])))
    }
    async fn hover(&self, _: HoverParams) -> Result<Option<Hover>> {
        Ok(Some(Hover {
            contents: HoverContents::Scalar(
                MarkedString::String("You're hovering!".to_string())
            ),
            range: None
        }))
    }
}
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let stdin = tokio::io::stdin();
    let stdout = tokio::io::stdout();
    let (service, socket) = LspService::new(|client| Backend { client });
    Server::new(stdin, stdout, socket).serve(service).await;
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub extern crate`- [lsp_types](https://docs.rs/lsp-types/0.94.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lsp_types/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [jsonrpc](https://docs.rs/jsonrpc/index.html)
- A subset of JSON-RPC types used by the Language Server Protocol.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html)
- Handle for communicating with the language client.
- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientSocket.html)- Socket
- A loopback channel for server-to-client communication.
- [Exited](https://docs.rs/struct.ExitedError.html)- Error
- Error that occurs when attempting to call the language server after it has already exited.
- [LspService](https://docs.rs/struct.LspService.html)
- Service abstraction for the Language Server Protocol.
- [LspService](https://docs.rs/struct.LspServiceBuilder.html)- Builder
- A builder to customize the properties of an `LspService`.
- [Server](https://docs.rs/struct.Server.html)
- Server for processing requests and responses on standard I/O or TCP.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Language](https://docs.rs/trait.LanguageServer.html)- Server
- Trait implemented by language server backends.
- [Loopback](https://docs.rs/trait.Loopback.html)
- Trait implemented by client loopback sockets.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/attr.async_trait.html)- trait
- A re-export of `async-trait`

# harn_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/harn-lsp/0.8.168/target-redirect/harn_lsp/

## Expand description

Harn language server.

Exposed as a library so the single multi-call `harn` binary can dispatch
into the LSP server when launched under the `harn-lsp` name (see
`harn-cli`’s `main`), instead of shipping a second fully-linked binary.
The thin `src/main.rs` shim keeps `harn-lsp` buildable as its own binary
for local development (`cargo run -p harn-lsp`).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Run the Harn language server over stdio until the client disconnects.

---

# harn_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-lsp/0.8.168/harn_lsp/index.html

## Expand description

Harn language server.

Exposed as a library so the single multi-call `harn` binary can dispatch
into the LSP server when launched under the `harn-lsp` name (see
`harn-cli`’s `main`), instead of shipping a second fully-linked binary.

for local development (`cargo run -p harn-lsp`).

- Run the Harn language server over stdio until the client disconnects.

[75](#75)mod tests {
[76](#76)    use super::*;
[77](#77)    use crate::helpers::{lsp_position_to_offset, word_at_position};
[78](#78)    use crate::symbols::HarnSymbolKind;
[79](#79)
[80](#80)    fn hover_symbol_at(
[83](#83)        source: &str,
[84](#84)        line: u32,
[85](#85)        col: u32,
[86](#86)        word: &str,
[87](#87)    ) -> Option<symbols::SymbolInfo> {
[88](#88)        let state = DocumentState::new(source.to_string());
[89](#89)        let position = Position::new(line, col);
[90](#90)
[91](#91)        let extracted = word_at_position(source, position);
[92](#92)        assert_eq!(
[93](#93)            extracted.as_deref(),
[94](#94)            Some(word),
[95](#95)            "word_at_position mismatch"
[96](#96)        );
[97](#97)
[98](#98)        let cursor_offset = lsp_position_to_offset(source, position);
[99](#99)
[100](#100)        let mut best: Option<&symbols::SymbolInfo> = None;
[102](#102)        for sym in &state.symbols {
[103](#103)            if sym.name != word {
[104](#104)                continue;
[105](#105)            }
[106](#106)            let in_scope = if sym.impl_type.is_some() {
[107](#107)                true
[108](#108)            } else {
[109](#109)                match sym.scope_span {
[110](#110)                    Some(sp) => cursor_offset >= sp.start && cursor_offset <= sp.end,
[111](#111)                    None => true,
[112](#112)                }
[113](#113)            };
[114](#114)            if !in_scope {
[115](#115)                continue;
[116](#116)            }
[117](#117)            match best {
[118](#118)                None => best = Some(sym),
[119](#119)                Some(prev) => {
[120](#120)                    let prev_size = prev
[121](#121)                        .scope_span
[122](#122)                        .map_or(usize::MAX, |sp| sp.end.saturating_sub(sp.start));
[123](#123)                    let this_size = sym
[124](#124)                        .scope_span
[125](#125)                        .map_or(usize::MAX, |sp| sp.end.saturating_sub(sp.start));
[126](#126)                    if this_size < prev_size {
[127](#127)                        best = Some(sym);
[128](#128)                    }
[129](#129)                }
[130](#130)            }
[131](#131)        }
[132](#132)
[133](#133)        best.cloned()
[134](#134)    }

[314](#314)            .find(|s| s.name == "add" && s.kind == HarnSymbolKind::Function)
[315](#315)            .expect("should find add");
[316](#316)        assert_eq!(fn_sym.signature.as_deref(), Some("fn add(a, b)"));
[317](#317)    }
[318](#318)
[319](#319)    #[test]
[320](#320)    fn hover_pipeline() {
[321](#321)        let source = "// Main entry point.\npipeline main() {\n  __io_println(\"hello\")\n}\n";
[322](#322)        let state = DocumentState::new(source.to_string());
[323](#323)        let sym = state
[324](#324)            .symbols
[325](#325)            .iter()
[326](#326)            .find(|s| s.name == "main" && s.kind == HarnSymbolKind::Pipeline)
[327](#327)            .expect("should find main pipeline");
[328](#328)        assert_eq!(sym.signature.as_deref(), Some("pipeline main"));
[329](#329)        assert_eq!(sym.doc_comment.as_deref(), Some("Main entry point."));
[330](#330)    }

[343](#343)
[344](#344)    #[test]
[345](#345)    fn hover_captures_flow_predicate_attributes() {
[346](#346)        let source = concat!(
[347](#347)            "@invariant\n",
[348](#348)            "@deterministic\n",
[349](#349)            "@archivist(evidence: [\"https://example.com/spec\"], confidence: 0.9, source_date: \"2026-04-01\")\n",
[350](#350)            "fn no_secrets(slice) -> bool {\n",
[351](#351)            "  return true\n",
[352](#352)            "}\n",
[353](#353)        );
[354](#354)        let state = DocumentState::new(source.to_string());
[355](#355)        let sym = state
[356](#356)            .symbols
[357](#357)            .iter()
[358](#358)            .find(|s| s.name == "no_secrets" && s.kind == HarnSymbolKind::Function)
[359](#359)            .expect("should find no_secrets");
[360](#360)        let names: Vec<&str> = sym.attributes.iter().map(|a| a.name.as_str()).collect();
[361](#361)        assert_eq!(names, vec!["invariant", "deterministic", "archivist"]);
[362](#362)        let block = crate::symbols::format_flow_attributes_block(&sym.attributes)
[363](#363)            .expect("flow metadata block");
[364](#364)        assert!(block.contains("@invariant"));
[365](#365)        assert!(block.contains("@deterministic"));
[366](#366)        assert!(block.contains("@archivist"));
[367](#367)        assert!(block.contains("evidence"));
[368](#368)        assert!(block.contains("https://example.com/spec"));
[369](#369)    }
[370](#370)
[371](#371)    #[test]

[374](#374)        let state = DocumentState::new(source.to_string());
[375](#375)        let sym = state
[376](#376)            .symbols
[377](#377)            .iter()
[378](#378)            .find(|s| s.name == "Repository" && s.kind == HarnSymbolKind::Interface)
[379](#379)            .expect("should find Repository interface");
[380](#380)        assert_eq!(
[381](#381)            sym.signature.as_deref(),
[382](#382)            Some("interface Repository<T> { fn map<U>(value, f) }")
[383](#383)        );
[384](#384)    }

# run in harn_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-lsp/0.8.168/harn_lsp/fn.run.html

`pub fn run()`## Expand description

Run the Harn language server over stdio until the client disconnects.

Builds a multi-threaded Tokio runtime and blocks on it, mirroring the
`#[tokio::main]` the standalone binary used. Called by the `harn-lsp`
binary shim and by the `harn` multi-call binary when invoked as `harn-lsp`.
